project.name: bits-reports
project.description: BITS reports — a full-stack campus IT support / incident reporting app (React frontend, FastAPI + Motor backend, MongoDB) with role-based workflows, Google sign-in, SLA monitoring and optional Gemini-assisted classification.

nodes.name: db.py
nodes.summary: Creates the shared Motor (async MongoDB) client and database handle from MONGO_URL/DB_NAME, builds all collection indexes (including TTL indexes for resets and security events) and initialises the database with retries and seed data at startup.
nodes.languageNotes: Module-level client and db objects act as a process-wide singleton; seed and logging imports are deferred inside init_db to avoid circular imports.

nodes.name: error_handling.py
nodes.summary: Request logging middleware and FastAPI exception handlers: tags every request with an X-Request-ID, writes one access line per request, and turns domain ITSMErrors, HTTP errors, validation errors and unhandled exceptions into clean JSON responses with explanatory log entries.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a contextvars-backed request context so log lines emitted anywhere during a request carry the request id and user.

nodes.name: logging_config.py
nodes.summary: Human-readable logging setup for the backend: console plus rotating app.log/errors.log files, secret redaction, project-relative tracebacks, and helpers that explain where an exception happened and how to fix common failures (MongoDB, SMTP, JWT, Gemini).
nodes.languageNotes: A contextvars.ContextVar carries per-request context into a logging.Filter, so the formatter can tag every line without passing request objects around.

nodes.name: campus.py
nodes.summary: BITS Pilani Hyderabad campus reference data (hostels, academic blocks) with regex rules that extract a location/room and estimate business criticality from free-text incident descriptions for form autofill.

nodes.name: scope.py
nodes.summary: Decides whether a report is an IT/facilities issue or a non-IT/emergency situation (medical, mental health, fire, electrical, security, pests) using deterministic keyword rules, and merges AI opinions with a safety-first rule so life-safety detections can never be overridden.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses frozen dataclasses, a str-valued Enum and leetspeak/Unicode normalisation before regex matching to make the keyword rules robust.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package marker for the FastAPI routers package; server.py imports the individual router modules from it.

nodes.name: client_errors.py
nodes.summary: FastAPI router that receives crash reports from the React frontend (render errors, uncaught errors, unhandled rejections), rate-limits them per IP and writes them to errors.log alongside backend errors.

nodes.name: docs.py
nodes.summary: Authenticated FastAPI endpoint returning in-app documentation about the incident lifecycle, the design patterns used and the intelligent features.

nodes.name: intelligence.py
nodes.summary: Core intelligence service: keyword and concept-based incident classification, category/service autofill, AI incident-detail generation through a Gemini adapter with strict reply validation, duplicate detection, scope assessment, technician recommendation, suggested resolutions and incident correlation clustering.
nodes.languageNotes: GeminiAdapter implements the IncidentClassifier ABC (Adapter pattern) and treats the LLM reply as untrusted input, clamping and defaulting every field; IntelligenceService takes a classifier factory for dependency injection in tests.

nodes.name: seed.py
nodes.summary: Idempotent database seeding: upserts default categories, services with criticality, settings, SLA policies following the project brief (upgrading old defaults), and demo admin, technician and student accounts.

nodes.name: ensure_indexes
nodes.summary: Creates unique, compound and TTL indexes on users, incidents, audit logs, notifications, password resets, SLA violations and security events, tolerating duplicate names on categories/services.

nodes.name: init_db
nodes.summary: Pings MongoDB with retries, ensures indexes and seeds default data, logging a warning per failed attempt and raising after the final one.

nodes.name: identify_user
nodes.summary: Derives a readable user label for log lines from the request's bearer token without failing on invalid tokens.

nodes.name: RequestLoggingMiddleware
nodes.summary: Starlette middleware that assigns a request id, sets the logging context, logs an access line with duration (flagging slow requests) and converts unhandled exceptions into a JSON 500 with a reference.

nodes.name: itsm_error_handler
nodes.summary: Converts domain ITSMError exceptions into JSON responses with their HTTP status and logs a hint plus the code location.

nodes.name: http_error_handler
nodes.summary: Handles Starlette/FastAPI HTTPExceptions, logging status hints and where the error was raised before returning a JSON body with the request id.

nodes.name: validation_error_handler
nodes.summary: Turns request validation errors into a readable list of problems, hiding values of sensitive fields such as passwords.

nodes.name: register_error_handling
nodes.summary: Registers the request logging middleware and all exception handlers on the FastAPI app.

nodes.name: is_sensitive
nodes.summary: Reports whether a field name looks like a secret (password, token, key, cookie and similar).

nodes.name: redact
nodes.summary: Recursively masks sensitive values inside dicts and lists before they are logged.

nodes.name: redact_url
nodes.summary: Removes credentials from a connection URL such as MONGO_URL before logging it.

nodes.name: short
nodes.summary: Truncates a value's string representation to a limit for compact log output.

nodes.name: format_traceback
nodes.summary: Formats a traceback with project-relative paths and highlights frames from the project's own code.

nodes.name: HumanFormatter
nodes.summary: logging.Formatter producing a one-line summary with timestamp, level, logger and request id, followed by an indented details block and traceback.

nodes.name: setup_logging
nodes.summary: Configures root logging with console output and rotating app.log/errors.log files under LOG_DIR, attaching the request-context filter and quieting noisy libraries.

nodes.name: where_in_code
nodes.summary: Finds the innermost project-code frame of an exception and returns it as file:line in function.

nodes.name: explain_exception
nodes.summary: Maps common exception types (MongoDB unreachable, SMTP, JWT, HTTP client, Gemini) to a plain-language explanation and a suggested fix.

nodes.name: log_exception
nodes.summary: Logs an exception with explanation, location, extra details and optional traceback at a chosen level.

nodes.name: extract_location
nodes.summary: Parses free text for a hostel or academic block and a room number, returning a structured location dict.

nodes.name: estimate_criticality
nodes.summary: Scores business criticality 1-3 from keywords: exams/payments/deadlines are critical, coursework is important.

nodes.name: Contact
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass holding an emergency contact's label, phone number and note.

nodes.name: ScopeKind
nodes.summary: String enum of report scopes: IT, facilities and the non-IT categories (mental health, medical, fire, electrical, security, pest, other).

nodes.name: ScopeAssessment
nodes.summary: Dataclass describing a scope decision (kind, source, matched words, in-scope flag, guidance and contacts) with a for_kind factory and to_dict serialiser.

nodes.name: normalise
nodes.summary: Lower-cases and Unicode-normalises text and collapses whitespace before rule matching.

nodes.name: rx
nodes.summary: Compiles a set of word patterns into a single case-insensitive regex with word boundaries.

nodes.name: RuleBasedScopeClassifier
nodes.summary: Deterministic offline classifier that strips IT idioms, checks scope rules in safety priority order and returns a ScopeAssessment, defaulting to IT.

nodes.name: parse_ai_kind
nodes.summary: Maps a free-form AI scope answer to a ScopeKind via direct value or aliases, returning None when unusable.

nodes.name: combine
nodes.summary: Merges the AI scope opinion with rule results, never letting the AI override a detected life-safety situation.

nodes.name: ClientErrorReport
nodes.summary: Pydantic model for a browser error report with bounded-length message, stacks, URL and reference fields.

nodes.name: report_client_error
nodes.summary: POST /api/client-errors handler that rate-limits by IP and logs the browser error with user, page, stack excerpts and a minified-build note.

nodes.name: docs
nodes.summary: GET /api/docs handler (signed-in users only) returning lifecycle, design-pattern and intelligent-feature documentation sections.

nodes.name: tokens
nodes.summary: Splits text into lower-case word tokens, dropping stop words and very short words.

nodes.name: keyword_count
nodes.summary: Counts whole-word occurrences of a keyword or phrase in text.

nodes.name: concepts
nodes.summary: Maps text to a set of stemmed concepts, merging synonyms so differently worded reports of the same failure overlap.

nodes.name: jaccard
nodes.summary: Computes the weighted Jaccard similarity between two concept sets.

nodes.name: dice
nodes.summary: Computes the weighted Dice coefficient between two concept sets.

nodes.name: DuplicateDetector
nodes.summary: Scores open incidents against a new report using title Dice and full-text Jaccard similarity plus a same-service bonus, returning those above the threshold.

nodes.name: IncidentClassifier
nodes.summary: Abstract interface for an external AI classifier that returns a classification dict or None.

nodes.name: GeminiAdapter
nodes.summary: Adapter wrapping Google's Gemini REST API: builds a sanitised prompt, sends the key in a header, retries server errors once, extracts JSON from the reply and validates/clamps every field, returning None on any failure.

nodes.name: IntelligenceService
nodes.summary: Facade over all intelligent features: category/service suggestions, scope assessment, AI or keyword classification, incident-detail generation, duplicate finding, technician recommendation, suggested resolutions and correlation clusters.

nodes.name: seed_all
nodes.summary: Upserts categories, services, settings, SLA policies (upgrading old defaults) and demo admin, technician and student accounts with hashed passwords.

nodes.name: server.py
nodes.summary: FastAPI application entry point: loads .env, sets up logging, logs a configuration summary, initialises MongoDB in the lifespan hook, runs the background SLA monitor loop, mounts all /api routers, error handling and CORS.
nodes.languageNotes: Middleware order is deliberate: error handling is registered before CORS so CORS is outermost and even 500 responses carry CORS headers.

nodes.name: log_configuration

nodes.name: InvalidStateTransitionError
nodes.summary: Raised when an incident is asked to move to a status its current lifecycle state does not allow.

nodes.name: TechnicianUnavailableError
nodes.summary: Raised when no technician has capacity or skills for an assignment.

nodes.name: MissingSlaConfigError
nodes.summary: Raised when no SLA policy is configured for an incident priority/service combination.

nodes.name: models.py
nodes.summary: Core OOP domain model of BITS reports: the abstract User hierarchy with polymorphic access rules, catalog value objects, incident parts (Location, Note, Resolution, Closure) and the Incident aggregate root that enforces lifecycle, SLA and assignment rules, plus User/Incident factories.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses read-only properties over private fields, frozen dataclasses for value objects and change tracking so repositories persist only modified fields.

nodes.name: User
nodes.summary: Abstract base for every actor, validating identity fields and defining polymorphic can_view/configuration permissions and Mongo document conversion.

nodes.name: Employee
nodes.summary: Customer (student/staff) user who may view only the incidents they reported.

nodes.name: Technician
nodes.summary: Support engineer with skills and a concurrent-workload limit; enforces capacity except for P1 incidents and restricts incident visibility.

nodes.name: Administrator
nodes.summary: IT manager user who can view every incident and manage system configuration.

nodes.name: SystemActor
nodes.summary: Singleton-style automation actor used for system-driven transitions such as classification and SLA escalation.

nodes.name: UserFactory
nodes.summary: Factory that validates role and email and builds the correct User subclass, both from parameters and from Mongo/API documents.

nodes.name: ItService
nodes.summary: Frozen value object for an IT service in the catalog, including its business criticality.

nodes.name: SlaPolicy
nodes.summary: Frozen value object for an SLA policy with response/resolution targets that can start the SLA clock for a new incident.

nodes.name: Location
nodes.summary: Validated incident location (online, hostel or academics) with formatting and document conversion.

nodes.name: Incident
nodes.summary: Aggregate root wrapping an incident document: keeps the State object in sync, tracks changed fields and notes, and exposes rule-enforcing operations for transition, classification, assignment, resolution, closure, SLA refresh and escalation.

nodes.name: IncidentFactory
nodes.summary: Factory that validates input and builds a brand-new Incident document in the NEW state.

nodes.name: state.py
nodes.summary: State pattern for the incident lifecycle: one IncidentState subclass per status declares which target statuses each role may move to, and StateFactory returns shared state instances.
nodes.languageNotes: Transition tables are expressed as class-level dicts mapping target status to allowed role sets.

nodes.name: IncidentState
nodes.summary: Base lifecycle state that validates a requested transition against its transition table and role permissions, raising domain errors on illegal moves.

nodes.name: StateFactory
nodes.summary: Registry-backed factory returning the singleton IncidentState instance for a given status.

nodes.name: strategies.py
nodes.summary: Strategy pattern implementations for incident priority calculation (matrix and weighted score) and technician assignment (skill, load, round-robin, experience, smart, priority-based), each selectable by name through factories.
nodes.languageNotes: AssignmentStrategy uses the Template Method pattern: select() is shared and subclasses only implement rank().

nodes.name: PriorityInput
nodes.summary: Validated dataclass of impact, urgency, business criticality, affected users and service criticality fed into priority strategies.

nodes.name: PriorityStrategy
nodes.summary: Abstract strategy interface for computing an incident priority from a PriorityInput.

nodes.name: MatrixPriorityStrategy
nodes.summary: Classic impact-by-urgency matrix mapping to P1-P4.

nodes.name: WeightedScorePriorityStrategy
nodes.summary: Computes a weighted score from impact, urgency, criticality and affected-user bonus, then buckets it into P1-P4.

nodes.name: PriorityStrategyFactory
nodes.summary: Name-keyed registry that returns a priority strategy and describes the available options for the admin UI.

nodes.name: TechnicianProfile
nodes.summary: Dataclass snapshot of a technician (skills, open workload, capacity, experience) used by assignment strategies.

nodes.name: AssignmentStrategy
nodes.summary: Abstract assignment strategy whose shared select() template filters by capacity (with P1 override) and picks the top-ranked technician from the subclass rank().

nodes.name: SkillBasedStrategy
nodes.summary: Ranks technicians by whether their skills match the incident category.

nodes.name: LoadBalancedStrategy
nodes.summary: Ranks technicians by lowest current open workload.

nodes.name: RoundRobinStrategy
nodes.summary: Rotates assignments across technicians, favouring the least recently assigned.

nodes.name: ExperienceBasedStrategy
nodes.summary: Ranks technicians by experience resolving incidents in the category.

nodes.name: SmartRecommendationStrategy
nodes.summary: Combines skill, load, experience, service familiarity and speed into a weighted score with a per-factor breakdown.

nodes.name: PriorityBasedStrategy
nodes.summary: Sends high-priority incidents to the most experienced technicians and lower priorities to the least loaded.

nodes.name: AssignmentStrategyFactory
nodes.summary: Name-keyed registry that returns an assignment strategy and describes the options for admin settings.

nodes.name: repositories.py
nodes.summary: Repository pattern layer encapsulating all MongoDB (Motor) access: a generic CRUD base plus collection-specific repositories for incidents, users, catalog, SLA policies, audit logs, security events, notifications and system settings.
nodes.languageNotes: Async Motor calls behind a shared abstract base keep persistence swappable without touching business logic.

nodes.name: MongoRepository
nodes.summary: Abstract async CRUD repository for one collection, converting ids to ObjectId and raising ResourceNotFoundError on misses.

nodes.name: IncidentRepository
nodes.summary: Incident persistence with sequential incident numbers, change-only saves, notes appending and open-workload queries.

nodes.name: UserRepository
nodes.summary: User lookups by email, active technicians/admins and public user listings.

nodes.name: SlaPolicyRepository
nodes.summary: Finds the SLA policy for a priority, preferring a service-specific policy over the default.

nodes.name: AuditRepository
nodes.summary: Audit log collection access, returning an incident's chronological audit trail.

nodes.name: SecurityEventRepository
nodes.summary: Records sign-ins and account-security events with client IP and user agent, and lists recent events per user.

nodes.name: SettingsRepository
nodes.summary: Single-document store of admin-configurable settings (strategies, escalation, correlation, admin 2FA) merged over defaults.

nodes.name: admin.py
nodes.summary: FastAPI admin router exposing administrator endpoints for managing users/technicians, IT services, categories, SLA policies, strategy and automation settings, audit logs and SLA violations, guarded by an optional admin-2FA requirement.

nodes.name: admin
nodes.summary: Dependency that requires the admin role and, when enabled in settings, an active authenticator app before allowing access to admin pages.

nodes.name: create_user
nodes.summary: POST /admin/users: creates admin or technician accounts via UserFactory after duplicate-email checks, storing a hashed password.

nodes.name: update_user
nodes.summary: PATCH /admin/users/{uid}: updates a user, validating changes through the domain UserFactory and normalising technician skills.

nodes.name: reset_two_factor
nodes.summary: POST /admin/users/{uid}/reset-2fa: clears a user's authenticator and backup codes and records a security event.

nodes.name: _validate_policy
nodes.summary: Validates an SLA policy input: resolution target not shorter than response, service exists and no duplicate priority/service policy.

nodes.name: put_settings
nodes.summary: PUT /admin/settings: validates and updates strategy, escalation and admin-2FA settings, returning available strategies.

nodes.name: audit_log
nodes.summary: GET /admin/audit: filters the audit log by incident number, action, actor and date range.

nodes.name: audit.py
nodes.summary: Backwards-compatibility shim re-exporting AuditRepository as AuditLogger; the audit trail now lives in the repositories module and is written by an observer.

nodes.name: incident_service.py
nodes.summary: Application service orchestrating the incident lifecycle: creation with scope/duplicate checks, priority calculation, SLA setup, correlation detection, search, manual and strategy-based assignment, transitions, notes, updates and SLA breach recording, publishing events to the EventBus.
nodes.languageNotes: Composition over inheritance: the service holds repositories, intelligence and an event bus, delegating rules to domain objects.

nodes.name: IncidentService
nodes.summary: Coordinates repositories, the intelligence service, settings-selected strategies and the EventBus to create, search, assign, transition, annotate and update incidents while domain objects enforce the rules.

nodes.name: test_domain.py
nodes.summary: Pytest unit tests for pure domain logic: priority strategy boundaries, priority input validation, lifecycle state transitions and role rules, and assignment strategy capacity and breakdown behaviour.

nodes.name: test_features.py
nodes.summary: Async integration tests (httpx ASGI client) covering the project-brief features: OOP domain factories and polymorphism, configurable strategies, audit trail, notifications, SLA monitoring and escalation, correlation alerts, suggested resolutions, search filters and admin configuration.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses module-scoped anyio fixtures and an in-process ASGITransport client against the real FastAPI app.

nodes.name: test_incident_factory_starts_new_and_lifecycle_is_enforced
nodes.summary: Verifies IncidentFactory creates NEW incidents and that Incident enforces legal transitions and roles.

nodes.name: test_creation_records_classification_priority_and_sla_in_the_audit_trail
nodes.summary: Checks that creating an incident records classification, priority and SLA entries in the audit trail.

nodes.name: test_admin_can_switch_assignment_strategy
nodes.summary: Verifies administrators can change the assignment strategy and it takes effect on auto-assignment.

nodes.name: test_notifications_reach_the_right_people_and_feedback_is_kept
nodes.summary: Checks observer-driven notifications reach reporters/technicians and that closure feedback is persisted.

nodes.name: test_sla_monitor_warns_records_violations_and_escalates
nodes.summary: Drives the SLA monitor through simulated time to verify at-risk warnings, violation records and escalation without duplicates.

nodes.name: test_sla_at_risk_warning_goes_to_the_technician
nodes.summary: Checks that an at-risk SLA warning notifies the assigned technician.

nodes.name: test_correlation_alerts_admins_once_and_lists_related_incidents
nodes.summary: Verifies correlated incidents trigger a single admin alert listing related incidents.

nodes.name: test_suggested_resolutions_come_from_similar_resolved_incidents
nodes.summary: Checks suggested resolutions are drawn from similar previously resolved incidents.

nodes.name: test_search_supports_many_filters
nodes.summary: Exercises incident search across many filter combinations.

nodes.name: test_admin_manages_services_categories_and_sla_policies
nodes.summary: End-to-end admin CRUD of services, categories and SLA policies, including in-use and default-policy guards.

nodes.name: test_missing_sla_policy_is_reported_clearly
nodes.summary: Verifies a clear MissingSlaConfigError when no SLA policy matches a new incident.

nodes.name: test_admin_edits_technicians_and_reads_audit_log
nodes.summary: Checks admins can edit technician skills/capacity and read the filtered audit log.

nodes.name: test_invalid_input_and_login_errors
nodes.summary: Verifies invalid input and bad login attempts produce the expected error responses.

nodes.name: security.py
nodes.summary: JWT and password security core: bcrypt hashing, access/refresh/MFA token issuance and decoding, token-version session revocation, and FastAPI dependencies that resolve the current user and enforce role-based access.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses FastAPI's dependency-injection via a closure factory (require_roles returns an inner async dependency) to build parameterised role guards.

nodes.name: schemas.py
nodes.summary: Pydantic request/response models for every API surface (auth, incidents, AI generation, admin catalog/SLA/settings, account security) plus clean_doc/serialize helpers that convert MongoDB documents to JSON while stripping private fields like password hashes and TOTP secrets.
nodes.languageNotes: Pydantic Field constraints (min_length, ge/le) declare validation rules declaratively on the model classes.

nodes.name: account.py
nodes.summary: FastAPI router for the signed-in user's account and security page: profile edits, password change, authenticator-app (TOTP) setup/enable/disable, backup codes, email preferences, sign-out-everywhere, and recent security activity.

nodes.name: hash_password
nodes.summary: Hashes a plaintext password with bcrypt and a fresh salt.

nodes.name: verify_password
nodes.summary: Checks a plaintext password against a stored bcrypt hash.

nodes.name: create_access_token
nodes.summary: Issues a 12-hour HS256 access JWT carrying user id, email, role and token version for revocation.

nodes.name: create_refresh_token
nodes.summary: Issues a 7-day refresh JWT bound to the user id and token version.

nodes.name: create_mfa_token
nodes.summary: Issues a short-lived (5-minute) MFA token proving the password step succeeded, valid only for submitting the authenticator code.

nodes.name: decode_token
nodes.summary: Decodes and verifies a JWT, mapping expired or invalid tokens to HTTP 401 errors.

nodes.name: public_user
nodes.summary: Projects a MongoDB user document into the safe public user dict returned to clients (id, role, skills, 2FA flag, etc.).

nodes.name: load_user_from_token
nodes.summary: Decodes a token of the expected type, loads the active user from MongoDB and rejects tokens whose version no longer matches (signed-out sessions).

nodes.name: token_from_request
nodes.summary: Extracts the bearer token from the Authorization header, falling back to the access_token cookie.

nodes.name: get_current_user_doc
nodes.summary: FastAPI dependency returning the full user document for the request's access token, or raising 401.

nodes.name: get_current_user
nodes.summary: FastAPI dependency returning the public view of the authenticated user.

nodes.name: require_roles
nodes.summary: Dependency factory that builds a guard rejecting users whose role is not in the allowed set.

nodes.name: serialize
nodes.summary: Recursively converts ObjectIds and datetimes to strings and strips private fields (password hashes, TOTP secrets, backup codes) from nested documents.

nodes.name: clean_doc
nodes.summary: Normalises a MongoDB document for API output by turning _id into id and serialising it safely.

nodes.name: overview
nodes.summary: Returns the account page payload: public profile, creation date, Google link status, 2FA status/requirement, email preferences and recent security events.

nodes.name: update_profile
nodes.summary: Validates and applies name/phone changes (blocking name edits for Google-linked accounts) and records a security-log event.

nodes.name: change_password
nodes.summary: Verifies the current password, enforces strength rules, stores the new hash, bumps token version to sign out other devices, alerts the user and reissues a fresh session.

nodes.name: start_two_factor_setup
nodes.summary: Generates a pending TOTP secret and returns it with an otpauth URI and QR code SVG for the authenticator app.

nodes.name: enable_two_factor
nodes.summary: Confirms the first authenticator code, activates TOTP, generates hashed backup codes and sends a security alert.

nodes.name: disable_two_factor
nodes.summary: Turns off the authenticator app after code verification unless admin 2FA is mandated, clearing secrets and backup codes.

nodes.name: regenerate_backup_codes
nodes.summary: Verifies an authenticator code and replaces the user's backup codes with a freshly generated, hashed set.

nodes.name: update_preferences
nodes.summary: Updates the user's email-notification preference and logs the change.

nodes.name: sign_out_other_devices
nodes.summary: Bumps the account token version to invalidate all existing tokens and reissues a session for the current device.

nodes.name: RegisterRequest
nodes.summary: Registration payload with name, email, password (min 8 chars) and optional phone.

nodes.name: LoginRequest
nodes.summary: Email/password login payload.

nodes.name: GoogleAuthRequest
nodes.summary: Google sign-in payload carrying the ID token credential and optional nonce.

nodes.name: PasswordResetConfirm
nodes.summary: Payload confirming an emailed password reset with email, code and new password.

nodes.name: AIGeneratedDetails
nodes.summary: Structured AI output for a drafted incident: title, description, category, priority, impact/urgency, tags, clarifying questions, confidence, scope, service and location.

nodes.name: SuggestRequest
nodes.summary: Report-form autofill request with title, description and candidate categories/services.

nodes.name: ScopeCheckRequest
nodes.summary: Request to check whether a report is in IT scope, with optional AI usage.

nodes.name: CreateUserRequest
nodes.summary: Admin payload for creating users with role, skills and max concurrent workload.

nodes.name: IncidentCreate
nodes.summary: Incident creation payload with title, description, category, service, impact/urgency, criticality and location details.

nodes.name: IncidentUpdate
nodes.summary: Partial update payload for incident fields such as impact, urgency, business criticality and affected users.

nodes.name: TransitionRequest
nodes.summary: State-transition payload with target status, resolution summary, root cause and feedback.

nodes.name: SlaPolicyInput
nodes.summary: Admin payload defining an SLA policy's priority, response and resolution minutes and optional service.

nodes.name: SettingsUpdate
nodes.summary: Admin settings payload selecting assignment/priority strategies, auto-assign, escalation, correlation parameters and admin 2FA requirement.

nodes.name: TwoFactorLoginRequest
nodes.summary: Second-step login payload with MFA token and authenticator/backup code.

nodes.name: AuthenticatorResetRequest
nodes.summary: Password reset payload authenticated by an authenticator code.

nodes.name: PasswordChange
nodes.summary: Password change payload with optional current password and new password.

nodes.name: auth.py
nodes.summary: FastAPI authentication router handling BITS-email registration, password login with optional two-step TOTP verification, emailed and authenticator-based password resets, Google ID-token sign-in, logout and the /me endpoint; issues JWTs as httpOnly cookies.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses UserFactory (Factory pattern) to create customer accounts and an SmtpEmailAdapter (Adapter pattern) to send reset codes.

nodes.name: catalog.py
nodes.summary: Small read-only catalog router listing IT services, incident categories, and active technicians (staff-only) for form pickers and filters.

nodes.name: incidents.py
nodes.summary: Incident REST router exposing list/search, create, detail (with allowed state transitions, audit trail and AI recommendations), transition, manual/auto assignment, notes and staff updates, delegating all logic to the IncidentService from the DI container.
nodes.languageNotes: Thin controller layer: every handler delegates to container.incident_service, keeping business rules in the service/domain layer.

nodes.name: extract_student_id
nodes.summary: Derives the numeric BITS student ID from an institutional email prefix.

nodes.name: issue
nodes.summary: Creates access and refresh tokens, sets them as httpOnly cookies and returns the token plus public user payload.

nodes.name: register
nodes.summary: Registers a student with a BITS Hyderabad email, building the customer user via UserFactory, then logs the event and issues a session.

nodes.name: login
nodes.summary: Password login that logs failures, blocks deactivated accounts, and returns an MFA token instead of a session when TOTP is enabled.

nodes.name: login_second_step
nodes.summary: Second login step that validates the MFA token, verifies the authenticator or backup code and issues the session.

nodes.name: request_password_reset
nodes.summary: Rate-limited password-reset request that emails a hashed six-digit single-use code, responding generically to avoid account enumeration.

nodes.name: confirm_password_reset
nodes.summary: Verifies an emailed reset code with attempt limits, sets the new password and revokes existing sessions.

nodes.name: reset_with_authenticator
nodes.summary: Resets a forgotten password using a TOTP authenticator code instead of email, revoking existing sessions.

nodes.name: google_auth
nodes.summary: Verifies a Google ID token server-side (issuer, verified email, nonce, BITS domain), links or creates the account and issues a session.

nodes.name: logout
nodes.summary: Clears the access and refresh token cookies.

nodes.name: me
nodes.summary: Returns the current user plus whether admin two-factor is required by system settings.

nodes.name: services
nodes.summary: Lists up to 200 IT services sorted by name for authenticated users.

nodes.name: categories
nodes.summary: Lists up to 100 incident categories sorted by name.

nodes.name: technicians
nodes.summary: Staff-only endpoint listing active technicians with skills for assignment pickers and filters.

nodes.name: listing
nodes.summary: Searches incidents with filters (status, priority, category, service, assignee, SLA status, scope, date range, escalation) via the incident service.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Creates an incident for customers or staff through the incident service.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Returns an incident with access checks, allowed state transitions, audit trail and, for staff, AI recommendations, related incidents and suggested resolutions.

nodes.name: transition
nodes.summary: Moves an incident to a new lifecycle state via the service's State-pattern transition logic.

nodes.name: assign
nodes.summary: Staff endpoint manually assigning an incident to a technician.

nodes.name: auto_assign
nodes.summary: Admin endpoint auto-assigning an incident using the configured assignment strategy.

nodes.name: note
nodes.summary: Adds a note to an incident's timeline.

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Staff endpoint patching incident fields such as impact, urgency and description.

nodes.name: intelligence.py
nodes.summary: Intelligence router exposing AI/rules-based helpers: incident classification, AI-generated incident details, duplicate detection, technician recommendations, incident correlation clusters, IT-scope checks and report-form autofill suggestions.

nodes.name: notifications.py
nodes.summary: In-app notifications router that lists a user's latest 50 notifications with an unread count and marks one or all notifications as read directly in MongoDB.

nodes.name: reports.py
nodes.summary: Reporting dashboard router whose single overview endpoint aggregates incident totals, status/priority/category/service breakdowns, SLA compliance, technician workload, recent SLA violations and correlation clusters for staff.

nodes.name: classify
nodes.summary: Suggests category, impact and urgency for free-text incident title and description.

nodes.name: generate_incident
nodes.summary: Generates structured incident details (AIGeneratedDetails) from a free-text description using AI.

nodes.name: duplicates
nodes.summary: Staff endpoint finding likely duplicate incidents for a title/description/service.

nodes.name: recommend
nodes.summary: Recommends technicians for an incident after verifying the caller can access it.

nodes.name: correlations
nodes.summary: Returns clusters of open incidents likely sharing a root cause, using configured correlation window and threshold.

nodes.name: scope
nodes.summary: Checks whether a report is an IT/facilities issue (rules-only or AI-assisted) and returns contacts for out-of-scope reports.

nodes.name: suggest
nodes.summary: Keyword-rule autofill suggesting likely categories and services for the report form.

nodes.name: listing
nodes.summary: Returns the user's 50 most recent notifications and the unread count.

nodes.name: read
nodes.summary: Marks one of the user's notifications as read, raising not-found for invalid or foreign IDs.

nodes.name: all_read
nodes.summary: Marks all of the user's unread notifications as read.

nodes.name: overview
nodes.summary: Aggregates incident, SLA, service, technician-workload, violation and correlation statistics into a single staff dashboard payload.

nodes.name: email.py
nodes.summary: Minimal SMTP email sender that delivers a plain-text message using STARTTLS and credentials read from SMTP_* environment variables, raising if email is not configured.

nodes.name: send_email
nodes.summary: Sends a plain-text email via SMTP with STARTTLS using environment-configured credentials.

nodes.name: container.py
nodes.summary: Composition root that builds every repository, service, notification channel and observer once and wires them together via hand-written dependency injection; exposes a module-level `container` singleton that routers import.

nodes.name: Container
nodes.summary: Composition-root class whose constructor instantiates all Mongo repositories, the TwoFactorService, the notification dispatcher with in-app/simulated/SMTP channels, the EventBus with its observers, IntelligenceService, IncidentService and SlaMonitor.

nodes.name: events.py
nodes.summary: Observer-pattern core: defines the incident event type enum, the immutable IncidentEvent payload, the EventObserver interface and the EventBus subject that fans published events out to subscribed observers.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a str-based Enum, a frozen dataclass with default_factory timestamps, and an ABC with an async abstract method.

nodes.name: EventType
nodes.summary: String enum listing every incident lifecycle and SLA event (created, assigned, resolved, SLA at-risk/breached, escalated, correlation detected, etc.).

nodes.name: IncidentEvent
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass carrying an incident snapshot, actor, description, previous/new state, extra data and a UTC timestamp for a published event.

nodes.name: EventObserver
nodes.summary: Abstract observer interface requiring an async on_event(event) handler.

nodes.name: EventBus
nodes.summary: Event subject that keeps (observer, type-filter) subscriptions and publishes each event to matching observers, isolating and logging individual observer failures.

nodes.name: sla.py
nodes.summary: SLA domain helpers: UTC time and datetime parsing, building an SLA record from a policy, the 25% at-risk window, and evaluating SLA status (on-track, at-risk, breached, met).

nodes.name: utcnow
nodes.summary: Returns the current timezone-aware UTC datetime; shared clock helper across the backend.

nodes.name: parse_dt
nodes.summary: Parses datetimes or ISO strings (including trailing Z) into timezone-aware UTC datetimes, returning None on invalid input.

nodes.name: build_sla
nodes.summary: Builds an SLA dictionary from an SLA policy and creation time, computing response and resolution due dates with ON_TRACK status.

nodes.name: at_risk_window
nodes.summary: Returns the timedelta covering the last 25% of the resolution window used to flag an SLA as at risk.

nodes.name: evaluate_sla
nodes.summary: Re-evaluates an SLA dict against now, computing response/resolution breach flags and the resulting MET, BREACHED, AT_RISK or ON_TRACK status.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package initializer marking backend/app/services as a Python package.

nodes.name: notifications.py
nodes.summary: Notification delivery layer: the Notification value object, an EmailSender interface with an SmtpEmailAdapter (Adapter pattern), pluggable in-app/simulated-email/SMTP channels and a NotificationDispatcher that fans out to all supporting channels.
nodes.languageNotes: Channels are polymorphic subclasses of an ABC; blocking smtplib is adapted to async via asyncio.to_thread.

nodes.name: Notification
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass describing a notification: title, message, kind, related incident and optional email subject/body.

nodes.name: EmailSender
nodes.summary: Abstract email-provider interface requiring async send and is_configured.

nodes.name: SmtpEmailAdapter
nodes.summary: Adapter implementing EmailSender by running the blocking send_email helper in a thread; configured only when SMTP env vars are set.

nodes.name: NotificationChannel
nodes.summary: Abstract notification channel with a supports() filter and an async send() method.

nodes.name: InAppChannel
nodes.summary: Channel that stores an unread in-app (bell icon) notification document in MongoDB.

nodes.name: wants_email
nodes.summary: Returns whether a recipient should get email for a notification: security alerts always, otherwise per the user's email preference.

nodes.name: SimulatedEmailChannel
nodes.summary: Channel that queues a simulated email in the email_logs collection for recipients who want email.

nodes.name: SmtpEmailChannel
nodes.summary: Channel sending real SMTP email only for selected kinds (resolved, SLA breached, escalation, security), logging sent/failed attempts.

nodes.name: NotificationDispatcher
nodes.summary: Sends a notification to a de-duplicated list of recipients over every channel that supports it, isolating per-channel failures.

nodes.name: observers.py
nodes.summary: Concrete incident-event observers: audit-trail writer, SLA violation register, and a notification observer that decides who is told what for each event type.

nodes.name: AuditObserver
nodes.summary: Observer that writes every incident event to the audit repository as a full history entry.

nodes.name: SlaViolationObserver
nodes.summary: Observer that records each SLA breach event as a document in the SLA violation register.

nodes.name: NotificationObserver
nodes.summary: Observer mapping each incident event type to recipients (reporter, technician, admins, escalation targets) and messages, sent via the NotificationDispatcher.

nodes.name: sla_monitor.py
nodes.summary: Background SLA monitor that re-evaluates open incidents, publishes at-risk and escalation events, records breaches and escalates unacknowledged P1/P2 incidents through three levels with auto-dispatch.

nodes.name: EscalationLevel
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass describing an escalation level: number, label, fraction of the response window and audience.

nodes.name: EscalationPolicy
nodes.summary: Policy defining Team Lead, System Administrator and IT Manager escalation levels and computing the highest level due for an unacknowledged incident.

nodes.name: SlaMonitor
nodes.summary: Periodic worker whose run_once refreshes SLAs of open incidents, publishes SLA_AT_RISK/ESCALATED events, saves changes, records breaches and auto-assigns escalated unassigned incidents.

nodes.name: two_factor.py
nodes.summary: TOTP two-factor authentication: Fernet-encrypted secrets, HMAC-hashed backup codes, QR provisioning, time-step matching, polymorphic TOTP/backup-code factors and a TwoFactorService with replay protection and brute-force lockout.
nodes.languageNotes: Codes are consumed with an atomic MongoDB conditional update (filter + update) so a code can never be replayed.

nodes.name: encrypt_secret
nodes.summary: Encrypts a TOTP secret with Fernet using a key derived from TOTP_ENCRYPTION_KEY or JWT_SECRET.

nodes.name: decrypt_secret
nodes.summary: Decrypts a stored TOTP secret, raising a user-friendly ITSMError when the server key has changed.

nodes.name: hash_backup_code
nodes.summary: Computes an HMAC-SHA256 of a normalised backup code so only hashes are stored.

nodes.name: normalise_backup_code
nodes.summary: Lowercases a backup code and strips non-alphanumeric characters for comparison.

nodes.name: new_backup_codes
nodes.summary: Generates N random 10-character backup codes in xxxxx-xxxxx form from a look-alike-free alphabet.

nodes.name: new_secret
nodes.summary: Generates a new random base32 TOTP secret.

nodes.name: provisioning_uri
nodes.summary: Builds an otpauth provisioning URI for the account with the BITS reports issuer.

nodes.name: qr_svg
nodes.summary: Renders arbitrary data as an inline SVG QR code string.

nodes.name: matching_step

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with README.md, which presents BITS reports as a full-stack campus IT reporting application for CS F213 built with a React frontend, a FastAPI + Pydantic + Motor backend and MongoDB. It covers manual and one-command setup, seeded admin/customer/technician accounts, Google sign-in, optional Gemini AI assistance and a feature-to-code map that the rest of this tour follows. The pinned requirements.txt shows the backend's building blocks at a glance: FastAPI/Uvicorn, Motor, PyJWT and bcrypt for auth, pyotp for two-factor auth, and pytest for testing.

tour.title: Backend Startup Sequence
tour.description: server.py is the FastAPI entry point and the most connected file in the graph: it loads .env, configures logging, initialises MongoDB in the lifespan hook, starts the background SLA monitor loop and mounts every /api router. db.py builds the shared Motor client, creates collection indexes (including TTL indexes) and retries initialisation before running seed.py, which idempotently upserts categories, services, SLA policies and demo accounts. error_handling.py and logging_config.py wrap every request with an X-Request-ID and turn failures into clean JSON responses plus human-readable log lines that explain how to fix common problems such as MongoDB or SMTP outages.
tour.languageLesson: FastAPI's lifespan hook is an async context manager: code before `yield` runs once at startup (connect to MongoDB, start background tasks) and code after `yield` runs at shutdown. Motor is the asyncio driver for MongoDB, so every database call is awaited instead of blocking the event loop.

tour.title: Composition Root (DI)
tour.description: Before looking at any endpoint, it helps to know where objects come from. container.py is the composition root: it builds every repository, service, notification channel and observer exactly once and wires them together with hand-written dependency injection, exposing a module-level `container` singleton. Routers import this singleton rather than constructing services themselves, so the whole object graph you will meet in later steps is assembled in this one file.
tour.languageLesson: Hand-written dependency injection means passing collaborators into constructors (e.g., a service receives its repository and event bus as arguments) instead of creating them internally. Keeping all of that wiring in one composition root makes swapping implementations, such as fakes in tests, a single-file change.

tour.title: Incident API and Security
tour.description: incidents.py is the REST surface for the core workflow: list/search, create, detail (with allowed transitions, audit trail and AI recommendations), transition, assignment and notes. It deliberately contains no business logic, delegating everything to the IncidentService obtained from the container in Step 3. Requests and responses are shaped by the Pydantic models in schemas.py, which also strip private fields like password hashes, while security.py provides bcrypt hashing, JWT issuance and the FastAPI dependencies that resolve the current user and enforce role-based access; auth.py uses those helpers for registration, login with optional TOTP, Google sign-in and password resets.
tour.languageLesson: FastAPI dependencies (`Depends(...)`) are functions that run before a route handler and inject their return value, such as the authenticated user. Chaining them (get current user, then require a role) gives declarative, reusable authorization on every endpoint.

tour.title: IncidentService Orchestration
tour.description: incident_service.py is the application service that the incidents router calls. It orchestrates the whole lifecycle: creation with scope and duplicate checks, priority calculation, SLA setup, correlation detection, search, manual and strategy-based assignment, state transitions, notes and SLA breach recording, publishing events as it goes. Think of it as the conductor: the next few steps open up each instrument it coordinates, namely the domain model, strategies, the event bus and repositories.

tour.title: Domain Model and State
tour.description: models.py is the OOP heart of the project: an abstract User hierarchy with polymorphic access rules, catalog value objects, incident parts such as Location, Note and Resolution, and the Incident aggregate root that enforces lifecycle, SLA and assignment rules. state.py implements the State pattern, with one IncidentState subclass per status declaring which target statuses each role may move to, served by a StateFactory. They share the vocabulary in enums.py (Role, IncidentStatus, Priority, SlaStatus) and raise exceptions from exceptions.py, whose ITSMError hierarchy carries HTTP status codes so the global handler from Step 2 can turn any rule violation into a JSON response.
tour.languageLesson: The State pattern replaces a large if/elif chain on `status` with one class per state, each answering 'where can I go next, and who may move me?'. Python's `abc.ABC` and `@abstractmethod` make the base class uninstantiable and force every subclass to implement the required methods, which is how polymorphism is enforced here.

tour.title: Priority and Assignment Strategies
tour.description: strategies.py provides the Strategy pattern for two decisions the IncidentService delegates: priority calculation (matrix or weighted score) and technician assignment (skill, load, round-robin, experience, smart and priority-based), each selectable by name through factories. Because the algorithm is chosen by name, administrators can switch it at runtime through admin.py, which exposes strategy and automation settings alongside user, service, category and SLA-policy management.
tour.languageLesson: A Strategy interface plus a Factory that maps a string name to a concrete class lets configuration (stored in the database) pick behaviour without the caller knowing which implementation it holds.

tour.title: Events, Observers, Notifications
tour.description: Whenever the IncidentService changes an incident, it publishes an event instead of calling side-effect code directly. events.py defines the immutable IncidentEvent, the EventObserver interface and the EventBus subject; observers.py supplies the concrete subscribers that write the audit trail, register SLA violations and decide who gets notified. notifications.py then fans each notification out over in-app, simulated-email and SMTP channels, using an SmtpEmailAdapter (Adapter pattern) around the minimal sender in email.py.
tour.languageLesson: In the Observer pattern the subject (EventBus) knows only the observer interface, so adding a new reaction to an event means registering a new observer in the composition root, with no edits to the service that publishes events.

tour.title: Repository Data Access
tour.description: repositories.py encapsulates all MongoDB access behind the Repository pattern: a generic CRUD base plus collection-specific repositories for incidents, users, catalog, SLA policies, audit logs, security events, notifications and settings. Services and observers from the previous steps talk only to these repositories, never to Motor directly, which keeps persistence details on top of the db.py connection from Step 2 out of the business logic.
tour.languageLesson: A generic base repository with shared create/find/update methods, subclassed per collection, is a classic use of inheritance for code reuse; the concrete repositories add only the queries specific to their collection.

tour.title: Intelligence and Scope Detection
tour.description: intelligence.py powers the 'smart' features: keyword and concept-based classification, category/service autofill, AI-generated incident details through a Gemini adapter with strict reply validation, duplicate detection, and technician recommendation. scope.py decides whether a report is an IT issue or a non-IT emergency (medical, fire, security and so on) using deterministic rules, and applies a safety-first merge so an AI opinion can never override a detected crisis. campus.py adds BITS Hyderabad hostel and block data to extract locations and estimate criticality, and the intelligence router exposes all of this to the report form; per the README, the app falls back to built-in rules when no Gemini key is configured.

tour.title: SLA Rules and Monitor
tour.description: sla.py holds the SLA domain helpers: building an SLA record from a policy, the 25% at-risk window, and evaluating status as on-track, at-risk, breached or met. sla_monitor.py is the background loop started by server.py in Step 2; it periodically re-evaluates open incidents, publishes at-risk and escalation events onto the EventBus from Step 8, records breaches, and escalates unacknowledged P1/P2 incidents through three levels with auto-dispatch.
tour.languageLesson: A long-running `asyncio` task started at application startup can loop forever with `await asyncio.sleep(...)` between passes, doing periodic work without a separate scheduler process.

tour.title: Frontend Shell and API Client
tour.description: On the browser side, index.js installs global error handlers and renders App inside an ErrorBoundary, while errorReporting.js sends crashes back to the backend's client-errors endpoint. App.js owns authentication state, the router, the login/2FA/Google sign-in screen and role-aware navigation. Every backend call goes through api.js, a shared axios client that attaches the bearer token, logs failures with backend request ids and clears the session on 401; in development setupProxy.js forwards /api to the FastAPI server so the app also works from phones on the same network.
tour.languageLesson: React ErrorBoundaries are class components that catch rendering errors in their child tree and show a fallback UI instead of a blank page. Centralising HTTP in one axios instance with interceptors means auth headers and 401 handling are written once for the whole app.

tour.title: Role-Based Pages
tour.description: The pages turn the backend concepts into screens. IncidentDetail.js shows an incident's lifecycle state, SLA deadlines and history, offering only the role-dependent transitions the State pattern allows; Dashboard.js visualises totals and SLA metrics from the reports endpoint; and AdminConfig.js lets admins choose the assignment strategy and priority algorithm from Step 7 and manage catalogue and SLA policies. common.js supplies the shared badges, modals and formatting helpers these pages reuse.

tour.title: Test Suite
tour.description: conftest.py isolates the pytest suite by forcing a throwaway itsm_test database, blanking SMTP and Gemini keys and providing a test JWT secret. test_domain.py unit-tests the pure domain logic (priority strategies, state transitions, assignment capacity), test_features.py drives the project-brief features end to end through an httpx ASGI client, and test_gemini.py exercises the Gemini adapter's edge cases with a mocked transport. Together they verify each pattern you have seen, from State and Strategy to Observer-driven audit and SLA escalation.
tour.languageLesson: pytest automatically loads conftest.py and shares its fixtures with every test in the directory, which makes it the right place to set environment variables before the application module is imported.

tour.title: Running the Full Stack
tour.description: Finally, see how everything runs together. docker-compose.yml starts MongoDB 7, the FastAPI backend on port 8000 and the React dev server on port 3000, with source bind mounts and a persistent mongo_data volume, building from the backend Dockerfile (python:3.12-slim running uvicorn). Without Docker, start.sh (and start.ps1 on Windows) performs one-command setup: it creates .env files from templates like backend/.env.example with a random JWT secret, maintains the virtualenv and node_modules, starts MongoDB and launches both servers.
tour.languageLesson: In docker-compose, services reach each other by service name on the internal network, which is why the backend's MONGO_URL points at `mongo` rather than localhost. Copying requirements.txt and installing it before copying the source keeps the dependency layer cached across code changes.
